Utilities¶

The utils subpackage provides tools for retrieving scientific reference spectra and processing Cloudy outputs into tables suitable for astrophysical HD/MHD codes.

Starburst99 Tables¶

Retrieve and load original Starburst99 tables with local caching.

class py4radiation.utils.sb99_retrieve.SB99Table(figure, path=None, refresh=False)¶

Bases: object

Retrieve and load pre-computed Starburst99 tables.

This class provides access to the original Starburst99 dataset presented by Leitherer et al. (1999).

Tables are downloaded on demand and cached locally to avoid repeated downloads. An existing local table may also be provided for use on systems without internet access.

Figures 1-12 contain spectral energy distributions (SEDs). Figures 7-12 include stellar emission only, they are recommended as input spectra for photoionisation models.

Parameters:
figure: str

Figure identifier from Leitherer et al. (1999), e.g. ‘8a’. The corresponding filename is constructed as ‘fig8a.dat’.

pathstr, Path or None, optional

Destination file path. If None, use the default cache directory provided by platformdirs.

refresh: bool, optional

If True, download a fresh copy of the table on the next retrieval, even if a cached copy exists. Default is False.

Attributes:
figurestr

Figure identifier.

pathPath

Absolute path to the local table.

urlstr

URL of the corresponding Starburst99 table.

References

Leitherer, C., et al. (1999), ApJS, 123, 3.

Examples

>>> table = SB99Table("8a")
>>> path = table.get_sb99table()
>>> data = table.load_sb99table()
get_sb99table()¶

Return a local Starburst99 table, downloading it when necessary.

If the requested table already exists and refresh is False, the existing file is returned without accessing the network.

When downloading, the table is first written to a temporary file and then moved into its final location.

Returns:
Path

Absolute path to the downloaded table.

Raises:
requests.RequestException

If the network request fails.

ValueError

If the download response is empty or does not contain the expected table data.

OSError

If the local table cannot be created or replaced.

load_sb99table(skiprows=3)¶

Load a Starburst99 table into a NumPy array.

Retrieve the table from the local cache, downloading it if necessary, and load its contents.

The default settings assume the format of the original Starburst99 SED tables (Figures 1-12), which contain three header lines.

Parameters:
skiprows: int, optional

Number of header lines to skip. Default is 3.

Returns:
numpy.ndarray

Starburst99 table with wavelengths in the first column and spectra at different stellar population ages in the remaining columns.

Notes

Other Starburst99 tables may require different parsing settings.

Haardt & Madau (2012) UV Background¶

Retrieve and load the Haardt & Madau (2012) UV/X-ray background.

class py4radiation.utils.uvb_retrieve.HM2012Table(path=None)¶

Bases: object

Retrieve and load the Haardt & Madau (2012) UV/X-ray background.

This class provides access to the CUBA ultraviolet and X-ray background spectrum produced by Haardt & Madau (2012), including emission from quasars and galaxies.

Tables are downloaded on demand and cached locally. An existing file may also be supplied for use in offline environments.

The original intensity values are returned without conversion to spectral flux densities. That conversion is performed separately by the SED class.

Parameters:
pathstr, Path or None, optional

Path to a locally stored UVB.out file. If None, use the default cache directory.

Attributes:
pathPath

Location of the UV background table.

localbool

True when an explicit local file was supplied. In this case, downloading is disabled if the file does not exist.

References

Haardt, F. and Madau, P. (2012), ApJ, 746, 125.

get_uvbtable()¶

Return the HM2012 table from local or download it.

If an explicitly supplied local file exists, return it without accessing the network.

If no local path was supplied, use the cached table or download UVB.out into the default cache directory.

Downloads are first written to a temporary file to avoid leaving incomplete data at the final destination.

Returns:
Path

Path to the existing or downloaded UVB.out file.

Raises:
FileNotFoundError

If an explicitly requested local file does not exist.

requests.RequestException

If the download request fails.

OSError

If the cached file cannot be written.

load_uvbtable_z(redshift_col=1)¶

Load wavelengths and specific intensities for one redshift column.

The original UVB.out file contains a numerical redshift header, followed by rows containing rest-frame wavelengths and specific intensities at the sampled redshifts.

The first spectral column contains wavelengths in Angstroms. The remaining columns contain J_nu in erg s^-1 cm^-2 Hz^-1 sr^-1.

The default redshift_col=1 selects z=0.

Parameters:
redshift_colint, optional

Zero-based column index corresponding to the desired redshift in each spectral data row. Defaults to 1, corresponding to z=0.

Returns:
numpy.ndarray

Two-dimensional array containing: - Column 0: rest-frame wavelength in Angstroms. - Column 1: specific intensity J_nu in erg s^-1 cm^-2 Hz^-1 sr^-1.

Raises:
ValueError

If the numerical redshift header is missing, empty, or does not begin at z=0.

Notes

The redshift_col argument selects a table column, not an arbitrary numerical redshift.

The current py4radiation workflow uses the z=0 spectrum.

Heating and Cooling Tables¶

PRocess radiative heating and cooling tables for HD/MHD codes.

class py4radiation.utils.hc_tables.HeatingCoolingTables(run_dir, run_name, loop_columns=None)¶

Bases: object

Combine radiative heating and cooling maps into a single table.

This class reads the master pyCIAO .run file and the individual heating/cooling maps produced by Cloudy.

For the default configuration, the output contains:

  1. Hydrogen number density [cm^-3].

  2. Temperature [K].

  3. Heating coefficient [erg cm^3 s^-1].

  4. Cooling coefficient [erg cm^3 s^-1].

  5. Mean molecular weight [amu].

The coefficient units above assume coolingScaleFactor=1, corresponding to normalisation of the volumetric heating and cooling rates by n_H**2.

Other coolingScaleFactor values require the appropriate interpretation of the resulting coefficients.

Parameters:
run_dirstr or Path

Directory containing the master .run file and heating/cooling maps.

run_namestr

Common simulation identifier. The ‘.run’ suffix may be supplied optionally.

loop_columnsSequence[LoopColumn] or None, optional

Loop parameters to include in the final table. By default, the ‘hden’ parameter is converted from logarithmic to linear hydrogen number density.

Attributes:
run_dirPath

Directory containing the input files.

run_namestr

Common identifier for the simulation run.

loop_columnstuple[LoopColumn, …]

Selected loop parameters included in the output.

write_table(outdir='.', outfile=None)¶

Write the combined heating/cooling table.

The individual Cloudy maps are processed in the order recorded in the master .run file.

All maps must contain identical temperature grids.

The resulting table is first written to a temporary file. The destination file is replaced only after every map has been processed successfully.

Parameters:
outdirstr or Path, optional

Directory where the combined table will be saved. Defaults to the current working directory.

outfilestr or None, optional

Output filename. If None, defaults to ‘{run_name}_cooltable.dat’.

Returns:
Path

Path to the generated heating/cooling table.

Raises:
FileNotFoundError

If the master .run file or a required data map is missing.

ValueError

If a data map is malformed or the temperature grids differ between runs.

Ionisation-Fraction Tables¶

class py4radiation.utils.ib_tables.IonTables(run_dir, run_name, elements)¶

Bases: object

Generate ionisation-fraction tables from pyCIAO/Cloudy outputs.

This class reads the established pyCIAO .run file and the ionisation-fraction maps generated for individual Cloudy runs.

The results are assembled into a multidimensional HDF5 table compatible with Trident.

The final dataset dimensions are ordered as:

(ionisation stage, density, redshift, temperature)

For calculations performed only at z=0, the ionisation grid is duplicated along the redshift axis, producing coordinates z=0 and z=1e-4.

The second redshift slice is introduced for Trident interpolation compatibility. It does not represent an independent Cloudy calculation or redshift evolution.

Parameters:
run_dirstr or Path

Directory containing the pyCIAO .run file and individual ionisation-fraction maps.

run_namestr

Common identifier for the simulation run. The ‘.run’ suffix may be supplied optionally.

elementsstr

Space-separated chemical element symbols to include in the final HDF5 table, for example ‘H C N O’.

Attributes:
run_dirPath

Directory containing the input files.

run_namestr

Identifier for the simulation run.

runfilePath

Path to the master .run file.

outfilePath

Path to the generated ionisation HDF5 table.

write_table()¶

Generate the HDF5 ionisation tables for the selected elements.

Each element is stored as a separate HDF5 dataset containing the logarithmic ionisation fractions.

The output file follows the naming convention:

{run_name}_iontable.h5

The file is opened in append mode. Existing datasets with the same element names are not overwritten automatically.

Raises:
ValueError

If no chemical elements were specified or the input parameter grids are inconsistent.

FileNotFoundError

If a required ionisation map is missing.
